summary.headline: Max Healthcare Q1 FY27 network revenue rose 16% YoY to INR 2,982 crore, while operating EBITDA margin slipped to 24.8% amid new capacity and oncology drug discontinuation.
summary.overview: Network gross revenue grew 16% YoY and 12% QoQ to INR 2,982 crore, with operating EBITDA up 15% YoY to INR 704 crore. Margin was flat YoY at 24.8% but down from 26.8% in the trailing quarter, which management attributed to new brownfield commissioning and the Kalinga (Max Bhubaneswar) acquisition. Net debt rose to INR 2,384 crore from INR 1,908 crore in March 2026, and free cash flow conversion was weak as receivables built up. Management guided that oncology normalises from Q3 FY27 and announced a medical education foray.

segments.name: Max Bhubaneswar (Kalinga, acquired)
segments.commentary: Post-acquisition contribution in Q1 was INR 19 crore revenue and INR 2 crore EBITDA, at 50% occupancy and ARPOB of INR 35,000. Pre-acquisition FY26 revenue was INR 154 crore.

segments.name: Oncology (in-patient)
segments.commentary: Share of in-patient revenue fell to 22% from 26% in Q1 FY26 after discontinuing select high-value chemotherapy drugs for institutional patients. Excluding oncology, gross revenue grew 20% and ARPOB grew 9% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Oncology expected to start normalising from Q3 FY27 and be fully normalised from Q4 FY27.
Max Smart's remaining 50% of the 400-bed brownfield tower to be handed over in Q1 FY27 (current quarter); Nanavati's remaining 50 beds also to be operational this quarter.
Management expects Smart and Nanavati EBITDA to ramp within 2-3 quarters of operations; Nanavati Phase 1 to achieve corporate-average margins without waiting for Phase 2.
Kalinga turnaround targeted within about 12 months, with occupancy and ARPOB targeted to rise 50-80%, plus 200-250 new beds.

Insurance: 6% automatic price revision expected at September-October 2026 renewals; CGHS super-specialty rates flowing from June, with INR 140 crore annual CGHS benefit tracking as roughly INR 35 crore per quarter from June.
Medical college plan: about INR 300 crore per 150-seat college, funded through internal accruals, with ROCE above 25-30% indicated; commercial operations expected over the next few years.
Net debt expected to rise marginally by year-end given capex; net debt/EBITDA targeted at 2.5x only if acquisitions are made.

Expansion pipeline: Max Lucknow +100 beds (next two quarters); Sector 56 Gurugram 500 beds phased from end-2026; Nagpur 100 beds and Zirakpur 400 beds in FY28; Pitampura 200 beds in FY29; Patparganj 400 beds by end-FY29; Dwarka 260 beds, Nanavati Phase 2 271 beds and Pune 450 beds by FY30.
capex_capacity: Max Vaishali: board approved INR 425 crore capex for a 202-bed brownfield tower, taking the hospital from 387 beds; construction started and commissioning expected before FY30. Management confirmed this is the same tower previously planned for FY29.
Max Smart: 50% of the 400-bed brownfield tower operational; beds opened are at about 80% occupancy with oncology focus.
Nanavati: remaining 50 beds operational this quarter; Phase 1 beds at about 80% occupancy; Phase 2 (271 beds) to take about 2.5 years and requires shutting about 100 beds.
Network free cash flow INR 397 crore; INR 337 crore invested in ongoing capacity projects and INR 386 crore on acquisitions (Kalinga and Yerawada).
Pune greenfield SPV acquired and now a subsidiary; 450-bed Pune project has IOD and is expected by FY30. Thane and Shaheed Path approvals: 30-36 months delivery after about six months of approvals.
demand_pricing: Occupancy stayed above 75% despite 13% YoY bed capacity growth.
Institutional (CGHS/PSU) share of in-patient revenue fell to 22%, and management said the decline will continue on current infrastructure.
Insurance negotiations ongoing with GIPSA and others; management denied any occupancy impact from insurer pressure on admissions.
Management said CGHS institutional business is loss-making on a fully loaded basis but contributes to fixed costs.
DSO rose to 95 days from 87 days, adding about INR 250 crore of receivables versus Q4 last year, mainly CGHS and PSU collections lumpiness; CGHS new portal is now processing bills.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Parliamentary Standing Committee's healthcare recommendation's impact and any reassessment of expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said the report is focused on affordability and that the company is not reassessing expansion; he said any viability issue could become a consolidation opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: Will Max Smart and Nanavati beds drive EBITDA quickly given 80% occupancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA should start rising by the second or third quarter of operations as ARPOB improves after occupancy ramps; Nanavati Phase 1 is already in that curve.

qa_highlights.question: What are the medical college economics and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated INR 300 crore for a 150-seat college, targeting ROCE above 25-30%, starting at Lucknow and funded fully from internal accruals. PG courses are also planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did FCF grow only 3% when EBITDA grew 15%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Yogesh Sareen attributed the gap to a receivables build-up (DSO 95 days vs 87), and a higher effective tax rate. FCF conversion was about 56% against the usual 62-65%; he expects normalisation as the new CGHS portal clears bills.

qa_highlights.question: Will oncology and institutional share recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Oncology is expected to normalise from Q3 FY27 and be fully normalised by Q4. Institutional share is expected to keep falling on present infrastructure.

qa_highlights.question: Will opex rise materially before Gurugram comes up?
qa_highlights.answer: Abhay Soi said indirect cost growth came from new capacity at Mohali, Nanavati and Smart plus Bhubaneswar; no major opex increase is expected, so revenue growth should flow to EBITDA.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from new brownfield capacity and Kalinga: EBITDA margin 24.8%, down from 26.8% in Q4 FY26.
Receivables (DSO 95 days) and CGHS collection lumpiness; FCF conversion about 56% vs usual 62-65%.
Kalinga minority shareholder (39% equity, based outside India) litigation over share purchase; company says it has full control.
Net debt up to INR 2,384 crore; management expects it to rise marginally by year-end while capex continues.
Parliamentary Standing Committee's 176th report on affordability and possible FDI caps; no hospital consultations so far.
Insurance renewals in September-October 2026 and whether the 6% automatic price revision holds.
summary.management_tone: Confident on capacity ramp-ups, the acquisition playbook and the medical education opportunity. More cautious and deflecting on CGHS economics, receivables and the Kalinga minority shareholder dispute, and it declined to give regional disclosure in the usual form.
key_quotes: We started the financial year with healthy momentum across the Network, recording year-on-year growth of 16% in revenue and 15% in operating EBITDA.
A hospital does not admit a patient, a doctor admits a patient.
We want to avoid giving solo hospital data.
So, one is that oncology will start to normalize from Q3 onwards.
